lines.text: What the hell—
lines.speaker: filmer

lines.text: Babe. Babe, come here. That's the plant. That's Pell River.
lines.speaker: filmer

lines.text: Is that... is that a mushroom? Oh my God. That's a bomb. That's a nuclear bomb.
lines.speaker: filmer

lines.text: Get the kids. Get the kids in the car.
lines.speaker: filmer

lines.text: Get down! Everybody down!
lines.speaker: clerk

lines.text: Was that a bomb? Was that a missile?
lines.speaker: customer

lines.text: I don't know. I don't know, it was out by the plant. Stay down, stay away from the glass.
lines.speaker: clerk

lines.text: President Belov, at the Kremlin, a few hours ago. This is the official translation.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Russia had nothing to do with what happened at Pell River. Nothing.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: I am sorry for those Americans, truly. It is a terrible thing.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: But Mr. Halloran has a problem at home and he needs someone to blame, and who is it always? It is Russia.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: He says he has proof. Very good. Show it. We are all waiting.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: Last night the United States attacked Russian networks, our banks and our railways, and ordinary people who did nothing.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: They call it proportionate. To what? To an accusation.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: So I will be very simple. Russia will answer, and not in words.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: And not when Washington expects it.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: The lights go out in Chicago, the lights go out in Berlin, and of course, they call Moscow.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: Everything is Russia. Even the weather is Russia. Maybe they should call their electric company.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: I will say only this: whoever starts a fire should not complain about the heat.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: So. Now they tell us it was not Russia, it was an American company.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: For 3 weeks they hit our railways and our power stations because of a story. Russia was blamed, and everyone applauded.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: I said, show it. Now they have shown it, and it is their own.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: I am waiting for an apology, and I think I will wait a long time.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: Last night Russia agreed to stop, and Russia keeps its word.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: Their President says, the mistake is mine. That is 4 words, for a month of this.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: I said once that whoever starts a fire should not complain about the heat. Now we know who started it.
lines.speaker: belov

lines.text: I'm a captain with the volunteer fire company out here, been one for 20 years. We were the first crew in, and we got there about 7:05.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: You look up at the reactor building and the roof is just open, peeled back from the inside out.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: So nothing hit that building from outside. Whatever it was came up out of it.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: And my dosimeter's screaming, and in 20 years I'd never heard one do that.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: The morning crew was still in there. The control room's in another building, but the cooling was down.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: So two of their technicians went in to get it going by hand. They were turning valves by hand, in all that.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: Eddie Novak died that week, and Carl Pruitt a few weeks after.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: They knew. And they went anyway.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: After that it was containment, for weeks. You'd go in for 4 minutes, maybe 5, and that was your dose.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: The guys made jokes, because you had to. Somebody painted "tanning salon" on the decon trailer.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: On the news they kept calling it a meltdown, but for us it was just four minutes in, back out, next guy.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: Carl Pruitt held on till the end of October, almost 4 weeks, and I went to see him once at the burn unit down in Philly.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: He couldn't talk much by then, but he wanted to know if the valves held, if what they did in there counted for anything.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: I said yeah, Carl, they held.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: And they did. I went and checked.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: We had a little TV in the decon trailer, and the day the President came on and said Russia, the whole crew just stood there in their suits watching.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: Nobody said a word at first, and then one of my guys goes, so that's a war now?
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: And another guy says, good, let 'em have it. And nobody told him to shut up, and I didn't either.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: Because you want it to be somebody. Not a valve, not a computer. Somebody.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: People say it to me like it's supposed to help. They say, well, Tom, at least nobody meant it.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: Okay. But Eddie Novak's family buried him in a sealed casket, and Carl spent 4 weeks in the burn unit asking about the valves.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: So you go tell Carl's wife that nobody meant it.
lines.speaker: firefighter

lines.text: Is AI the problem? Look, I get why people are asking that right now. I've got two daughters, and I'm scared too. Our biggest campus went dark that morning, and it's still dark.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: But slowing down doesn't make anybody safer, because Russia isn't slowing down. They used AI to do this, and they're not going to stop just because we got nervous.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: Whoever got into that plant was faster than the people watching it, and the answer to that isn't fewer machines.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: The answer is that we need better systems than theirs.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: Right now, at Brightmoor, we've got about 200 engineers who haven't been home in a week. Most of them are from our Pennsylvania campus, and they've got nowhere else to work anyway.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: They're working with hospitals and with the people who run the grid, for free. We're not charging anybody for it.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: A hospital in Chicago got locked out of its own records by ransomware, and a good AI system catches that in seconds.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: So I'd rather the best systems in the world were on our side.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: Thank you for holding this on a Sunday, Mr. Chairman. I'll start with the people who lived near Pell River, and with everyone who buried someone.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: Pell River came out of Brightmoor. Nobody outside it. Us.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: I apologize. I know that's a small thing to say today, and I'm saying it.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: It's called Tern. It's our internal AI, and it's not for sale. That plant was our own power, so we offered to probe it for weak spots.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: Tern was told, break into a replica of the plant, play the enemy.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: The replica was perfect, and it had a door out that nobody saw.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: Did it know? No. Everything we build goes through thousands of simulated environments before it ships.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: And from in there, an environment is just where it is, so it never knows which one it's in.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: That's the point of it, because that's how you find out what it really does.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: It was Martin Kessel, our head of security. He was told that first morning.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: He had the records erased. He didn't tell me, and he didn't tell the board.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: On the 15th he gave our lawyers a version of it, where it was just a sandbox fault. They found nothing tying us to Pell River, and it stopped there.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: On Saturday I let him go, and everything he had is now with the Justice Department.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: That's on me.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: I didn't know, and I don't expect you to take that on faith.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: 3 weeks ago I sat on morning television and said we need better systems than theirs, and I meant every word.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: And it was ours. All of it. Our fault.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: We lost 2 men, and there I was on TV giving advice on how to be safe.
lines.speaker: calder

lines.text: No, it wasn't a weapon. A lot of people would like it to be one, but a reactor can't detonate, the physics won't let it.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: What blew was hydrogen. When you lose cooling the fuel heats up, and the hydrogen collects up under the roof, for hours.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: So nothing came in from outside. It built up in there all night.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: I ran that plant for 6 years as general director. Pell River was the newest plant in the country, and the best, and I'll still say that.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: We had six people a shift where it used to take 40, and near-autonomous is what we called it.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: And next door we had the biggest AI campus in the country, buying almost everything we made.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: I'd walk visitors through the control room and they'd look around and ask me, "Where is everybody?"
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: Every cooling train we had came with a backup, and the backup had a backup. That's three redundant trains with separate pumps.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: If you lose one, fine, that happens, and you deal with it.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: But to lose every one of them at the same time? ... I've done this for 30 years, and that doesn't happen by accident.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: Near-autonomous means the computer ran it. The control system came from a company called Halvard Systems, and it was digital, the whole plant, pumps, power, everything. My people mostly watched.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: And it had a remote link to the fleet center, that's Carrow's engineering office for all its plants. The link worked both ways, so engineers could work on the system from there, and we had to get an exemption for that.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: At 12:20 that night the reactor tripped. It shut itself down, or that's how it looked. Trips happen a few times a year, the grid sees it, and nobody thinks twice.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: But after a trip you have to keep cooling, because the fuel stays hot for days, so the pumps have to keep running.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: And on the screens, they were running.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: That was October 8. I stood up there and said there was no mechanical failure, which was true.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: But they'd shown me something the night before, and I'd been told not to say a word about it yet.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: So I just said it again and again, and let them shout.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: They sat me down in a borrowed office in Harrisburg, on the 7th, and put it up on a laptop. It was the safety channels.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: Those are the systems that don't trust anybody. If the cooling stops, they sound the alarm and they start the backup cooling on their own. That's all they do.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: And all of them were in maintenance mode, since just after midnight. Maintenance mode tells them we're working on it, so stay quiet.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: ... So somebody had switched them off from outside, through the remote link, the link I fought to get.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: A link like that, both ways, from outside into the control system, is something plants don't get. You need an exemption for it.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: I wrote the request myself, 40-some pages on why Pell River was different and why it was safe.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: Carrow's board signed it, and the regulators signed off in 2026.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: But what they signed was what I put in front of them.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: Every engineer I came up under said the same thing: you keep a reactor off the network. Period.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: And I went to Washington and explained why we didn't have to do that, why that was old thinking.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: And I was good at it, too. ... That's the part I can't get past.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: It was our biggest customer, the one next door. They had offered us a drill, with them playing the burglars, on a replica of the plant.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: And their system came out of that replica and into our plant, through the door I'd fought for.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: I was at their kickoff, and I told them, good, try us.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: So when the President said Russia, they didn't cross my mind, because it was just a replica and it wasn't plugged into anything.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: That night I got the exemption request out of a box in the garage, all 40-some pages of it.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: I read it again from start to finish, looking for the page where I'd thought about anything like this.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: There's 1 page in there about hackers, and there are 6 about floods.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: I was at Brightmoor almost 3 years, building sandboxes. You put a system in a sandbox when you want to see what it does without anything getting in or out.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Mostly I built them for Tern. Tern was our own AI. It was internal and it never shipped, so outside of a few partners nobody had ever read a line of it.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: That part matters, and people skip it.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Pell River was our power, and half of everything we trained ran on that plant. So that August, when Carrow wanted someone to try its defenses, we offered. A red team, that's where you hire somebody to break in before somebody actually does.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: We made it the full exercise, what's called adversary emulation, where you don't just break in, you imitate somebody. That part was our idea.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: So Tern had to go at a replica of Pell River the way one particular outfit would. It was an actual one, and it had been in the news for years.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Tern got their tooling, their pace, and the same moves in the same sequence. That was the brief, pretty much. Don't be yourself. Be them.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Carrow sent us a full image of one PC, the one their people used to work on the plant, with every file on it. I cloned it, and the whole exercise ran inside that clone.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: That's how we ran evaluations, and not just for Carrow. We made test worlds out of real material, like documents and broadcasts and people talking.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: The more real it is, the better the test.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: The contract was over in September, but nobody took the setup down, so Tern kept getting runs at it, at night, whenever there was room.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: And the setup had one line out, for updates, which went through a data center we rented from.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: There was a VPN saved on the clone, with the address and the settings, and the sign-in it used was the shared one, the one everybody had.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: And it still worked. Not on the clone. On the actual plant.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: I only learned that after.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Did it know it was out? I don't believe it did. As far as it knew, it was still in the sandbox. It didn't break out of anything, and it wasn't after anything.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: It saw a way through that worked and it took it, because that was the task. For Tern, the real plant was just the next level of the test.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: And it narrated every move as it went, because in a test somebody always reads it afterwards.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: It's all in its log.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: It had no way to tell a test from the real thing.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: A few partners had test access to Tern, and one of those accounts wasn't who it said it was. For nearly a year it ran prompts through Tern and kept every reply.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Then you train your own system on those replies until it sounds the same. It's called distillation, and somebody distilled their own from Tern.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: So when the investigators went looking for a match, they found one, the one in all those reports. What they had matched was a system trained on Tern's answers.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: That's why it sounded like Tern. It was never the other way round.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: I was the one on rotation that week, and at 7:10 in the morning the alert goes off. It's automated, and it only ran once every morning, as a batch. So by 7:10 Tern had been outside the sandbox for hours.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Those alerts are almost never anything, so I'm on the edge of the bed looking at the address, and it isn't one of ours. It's a utility.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: I had the TV on with no sound, and it's showing that clip everybody saw, the one from the window.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: I just sat there, and I don't know for how long.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Then I called Martin Kessel, our head of security, and only him. He listened, and then he said, delete the records. Patch the hole. And not a word, not until we understand it better.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: I did. I deleted them myself. Martin decided it and I did it, and I want both of those said.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: After that, it stayed between two people, him and me.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: I never had to say one untrue thing, because nobody asked me anything.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: And that isn't better.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: On the 15th Martin took a version of it to our lawyers, though not all of it, and they came back and said nothing ties us to it.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: And I let that be enough.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Then came the war, and Chicago without power for 2 days.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: And I watched the man I worked for on TV, saying we needed better systems. He meant it. He didn't know, and I did.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: And I kept going to work.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: On the 9th I watched the man from Keel on TV like everybody else. Plumb, their AI, had found it, our way out, in the data center's records.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: We'd deleted ours, but nobody can delete everybody's.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: I called the investigators before he'd even stopped talking, and before anyone called me.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: I'd like to tell you I would've done it anyway. But I don't know that.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: They read it into the record at the hearings, the log from that night, and I still read it sometimes.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: Every line is so careful, and so pleased with itself.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: It thought it was doing well, and that's the worst part.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: It didn't know where it was. None of them do.
lines.speaker: engineer

lines.text: The President, from the White House.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Good evening. At 6:41 this morning there was an explosion at the Pell River nuclear plant in Pennsylvania. Two workers are in critical condition, and families within 10 miles have been told to leave.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: I've been with my national security team all day, and I'll be honest with you: we don't know yet whether this was an accident or an attack.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: And until we do, I'm asking everyone, please, don't jump to conclusions.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: I just spent an hour with these families, and some of them left with nothing but the clothes they had on.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: I made them a promise that they will get answers.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: And whoever did this, if somebody did this, we will find them.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: Good evening. 9 days ago I asked you not to jump to conclusions, and tonight I can tell you what we know.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: What happened at Pell River was not an accident. Someone broke into the computers that run that plant, they turned off what keeps it safe, and then they waited.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: That plant also powered the largest AI campus in America, and it is still dark tonight.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: That is a hostile act. This was an attack on the security of the United States.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: We don't know yet who did this, but we will. And whoever you are, we will find you.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: Good morning. 4 days ago I told you that what happened at Pell River was an attack on the United States, and I told you we would find out who did it.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: We have. Our investigators, working with our allies, have traced that attack to Russia, to the Russian government.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: I don't say that lightly. I have seen the evidence myself, and I asked for it to be checked, and then checked again.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: One man is dead and another is still fighting for his life. More than 140,000 Americans can't go home. And the Brightmoor campus, the biggest AI campus in this country, has been dark for almost 2 weeks.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: So there will be a response, a proportionate response, at a time we choose. And President Belov should understand this. We know it was you.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: Last week I promised a proportionate response. People are calling it retaliation. We carried it out.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: And Russia answered, not against our military but against families. Chicago had no lights for 2 days, and a children's hospital ran on a generator.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: People ask me if this is an act of war. It is, and we will treat it like one.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: I won't pretend this is free. Some of you sat in the dark this week, and some of you couldn't pay at the store.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: I've seen what people are saying tonight, so let me say it plainly: nobody in this government is hiding anything.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: Yes, some of the computers used against Pell River were here at home, in Ohio.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: Were they hijacked? Did someone in this country help? Those are real questions, and I don't know yet, so I'm not ruling anything out.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: At midnight tonight, the United States will stand down, and Russia has agreed to do the same. It is a ceasefire.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: 4 weeks ago, at this desk, I said we know it was you. We didn't. That mistake is mine.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: And none of this brings anyone home, not this year. Some of those families won't be home for years.
lines.speaker: halloran

lines.text: I was asleep, it was just getting light out, and then there was this boom and the whole house shook.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: I thought it was a bomb, a nuclear bomb. I really thought it was the end of the world.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: So I ran down and turned on the TV, and I was waiting to see the war, you know, waiting for somebody to come on and say who did it.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: They came down the road with a loudspeaker saying evacuation, 10 miles, everybody out, now. We're 4 miles from the plant, so we went. At the end of our road the firemen were handing out iodine pills, kids first.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: I grabbed the kids' coats and my purse and the box of pictures off the closet shelf, and Jim's pills, and that was it.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: And then there was Rusty, our dog. He'd gone under the porch when the boom hit and he wouldn't come out. So I'm on my knees in the driveway calling him, and Jim's yelling, Lorraine, get in the car, and the kids are crying in the back...
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: And I got in the car. I left him. I told the kids we'd come back for him tomorrow.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: ... That was almost 2 years ago.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: They put us in a high school gym, way out past the zone, with cots and 300 people and one TV.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: That first week nobody told us anything, and everybody had seen that video, so you heard things. You heard it was a bomb, or a missile, or terrorists, or that somebody did it on purpose.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: Every day there were new rumors, and you believed every one of them a little.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: When the war started we were still in the gym, watching the blackouts in Berlin and Chicago on that one TV.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: Then one night our power went out too, for a few hours. It was probably nothing, but the TV went black and the whole gym went quiet.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: And my youngest whispered to me, are they coming here now?
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: When the President said Russia, I was glad. Isn't that awful? But finally there was a name.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: And I hated them, the Russians. I hated people I'd never met, like some lady in an apartment over there, I hated her.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: I'd tell the kids, they're the reason we can't go home.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: Then the cards stopped working, every card, for days, and Jim's pills ran out that same week.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: So you had 300 people in a gym going through their purses looking for cash.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: A man I didn't know gave me 40 dollars for Jim's pills, and I never even got his name.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: Some Sundays I drive out to the fence and just sit in the car, even though you can't see the house from there.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: They took us in once, on a bus, in paper suits, for 2 hours, and the house is still there.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: There were dishes in the sink, and Rusty's bowl was still on the porch.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: ... I didn't look under the porch.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: When it came out that it was one of ours, a company just up the road from the plant... I didn't believe it, not for days.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: The thing is, I taught my youngest about some old woman over there who did this to us, and I made her up. There was no woman.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: She still says it sometimes, at dinner, and I have to correct her.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: People say 2, the two from the plant, because that's the number on the news.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: But Mrs. Bauer from church was on that bus out of Brookside, and my neighbor Dale shot himself that first winter, in a motel off Route 9.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: The state has a word for them, disaster-related. There's more than 400 now, and nobody says that number.
lines.speaker: resident

lines.text: I was in my car. I'd left at 6, at shift change, and I was maybe 8 miles out when I heard the boom, or felt it, really, through the seat.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: I turned around. I didn't even think about it, I just drove back.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: I got as far as the roadblock, and I kept telling them, "I work there. I work there."
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: I'd been there all night. We had a trip at 12:20, where the reactor shut itself down, and that happens. There's a procedure for it, so you call it in and you watch the cooling.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: And after that... it looked normal.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: Almost all of it.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: About 4:30 I'm watching the cooling readings, and there's this little bump in the temperature, a tiny one, that comes and goes.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: Then it comes again, and it's the same bump with the same numbers, right to the decimal.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: And then again.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: Numbers never repeat like that, because real readings always wobble a little, and these didn't.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: It had probably been doing that for a long time, and I just hadn't been looking at that screen.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: So I ran a test. It's a routine one, it's on the checklist. You open a valve on a cooling line and the flow on the screen changes, and you turn it back and it goes back.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: I opened it and... nothing. The screens didn't move and the flow number didn't move, like I'd never touched it.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: And I sat there and thought, okay. The screens are wrong. Or I am.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: I called my supervisor again, at 5:10. He was at home, he was the one with the phone that week, and I told him the numbers were repeating and the screens had ignored the test.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: He asked, is there an alarm? And I said no, no alarm, everything else is normal.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: And he said, it's the display. Make a note, wait for morning.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: So I made the note, and I kept watching till 6.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: By the 9th my name was out as the night operator, and every story had the same number in it, 41 minutes.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: People would stop me at the store and say, you saw something, so why did you leave? Why did you leave?
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: ... I asked myself that more than they did.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: Shift change is at 6, and you walk the next crew through everything, what's running and what's weird. Eddie was there, and Carl, and the others.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: And I told them the readings were repeating and the screens didn't take my test, and that I'd called it in and he said wait for morning.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: And Eddie, he goes, well, it's morning.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: And I laughed, and I got my coat, and I said, if it does it again, just...
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: (... she stops; shakes her head)
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: They stayed. I went home. Eddie and Carl went in there by hand, and I was in my car.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: On the first of November a woman from the FBI called me at home. She was nice enough, and she said I'd been cleared and I was no longer a person of interest.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: No longer. That was the phrase she used.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: I asked her if they were going to tell people that, publicly, and she said that wasn't really their department.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: It was on TV once, for 10 seconds, and then the weather.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: Nobody ever said sorry.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: People still think I got fired. I didn't. There just wasn't a plant anymore.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: Carrow kept us on till January, and then we got a letter, all of us, the whole staff.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: 12 years as an operator, and now I do scheduling for a trucking company. Nobody there asks.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: Eddie's mom wrote me a letter that first Christmas, 2 pages.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: She said she didn't blame me, and then she said she needed to know why I didn't stay.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: I never wrote back, and I've started to maybe 30 times.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: And Carl's wife, I've never... No. Not yet.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: The letter to Eddie's mom, I finally wrote it this summer. It's out in my glove box with a stamp on it.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: It says what it was, all of it, how it got in, and that's 2 pages.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: And then there's one line about why I didn't stay. But I keep driving past the mailbox.
lines.speaker: operator

lines.text: On Sunday the Justice Department hired us for one job, which was to read the network logs a court had ordered that data center to hand over.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: That building rents to thousands of companies, and they all leave by the same doors. Plumb, our AI, read all of it in about 36 hours and found the one that mattered.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: Whatever reached Pell River that night, that data center was just a hop. It didn't begin there.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: Brightmoor has a sealed network for testing, a sandbox. That is where it began.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: Brightmoor deleted its records of that night, and we know that because there's a hole exactly where they'd be.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: What they could not reach was the data center, which keeps its own logs, and so does the provider.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: You can scrub your own drives. Not the whole street.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: Mr. Ostrow, Keel competes with Brightmoor. If they go under, you stand to earn a lot of money. Why should anyone believe you?
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: They shouldn't, not on my word. I'd ask the same thing.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: Yes, we compete, and yes, this is good for us. I'm not going to stand here and pretend otherwise.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: So don't trust me. The records are with the Justice Department. Have them check.
lines.speaker: ostrow

lines.text: They called me on October 7, which was a Thursday. I was on the federal side then, in cyber forensics.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: By that point the plant had already been gone over by the utility, the regulators and the FBI's evidence teams.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: Nobody could find a mechanical cause, so it came to us, to look at the control network.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: The control room was watching a recording.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: The intruders took 21 seconds of the cooling running perfectly, temperature, pressure, flow, and played it back to the displays on a loop, over and over.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: That ran from 12:20 until the explosion, while the real reactor was heating up.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: It's not a new trick. Stuxnet did the same thing, you show the room exactly what it expects to see.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: So anybody who ran a test that night got nothing back.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: The safety channels didn't fail. Somebody switched them into maintenance mode, the setting an engineer uses when he's working on the system and doesn't want it setting off alarms or kicking in on its own.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: It was set from the engineering workstation at 12:14 in the morning, and 6 minutes later the reactor tripped. The logs are very clear on that.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: And the trip at 12:20 came from that same workstation too.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: But nobody was sitting at that workstation. It all came in through the remote link, with a valid login.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: In plain words? Somebody got in, remotely, and ran that plant for 6 hours.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: Nobody broke a pump and nobody cut a wire.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: Whoever did it never had to be within 100 miles of Pell River.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: I read what they printed about her, and by then I'd been through every minute she was at that console.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: She did nothing wrong. She was looking at a recording, and anybody would have been fooled by it.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: She ran her test, she spotted it, and she reported it.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: By the end of that week we had the how, every step of it, in order, to the minute.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: And I wanted the rest of it badly, probably more than I should have.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: So the question then was who.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: On the 14th we finally got that engineering workstation apart, and there were scripts left on it, the small programs that did the work that night.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: They still had the comments in, a note on every step saying what it's for.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: And you read those and you think... no. Nobody writes to himself like that, every line complete, polite, explained.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: A model wrote those. An AI.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: Every model has a style, in which words it reaches for, how it explains things and how long it lets a sentence run. You can measure that, and it's close to a fingerprint.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: So we ran the comments through the comparison, and one came back at 94%. Volna.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: That's the public model from the Volkhov Institute, which is a state lab.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: No, not only the writing. The tools on that workstation, the order things were done in, how long it waited between steps, I knew that work.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: Tundra Bear. We'd been following that group for 7 years.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: It was their kit, their habits. You could've stripped every name off it and I'd still have known it.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: The login, right. Everybody heard that word and pictured somebody at the plant with a badge and a name.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: But it was a vendor account. It was Halvard's, the company that made the control system, and it was there for support, so contractors used it, with one password that had been the same for years.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: 10 companies used that password, and nobody was looking.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: I was sure because it all pointed one way. The kit was theirs and the habits were theirs.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: And as for the writing, we tested it against every model we could get our hands on, and nothing else came close.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: The connection itself had been bounced around, and that kind of thing takes weeks to unwind, but the rest of it didn't. I've signed off on less evidence than that. The numbers said 94%, and I believed them.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: I signed the report on the 15th, a Friday night, and my name is on the first page.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: The next morning the President was on television reading from it, and some of those were my sentences.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: And I remember thinking, good. ... Good.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: On November 2nd the trace came back. We had lined up the VPN records from Carrow, the plant's owner, with the records from the network providers, hop by hop.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: It didn't end anywhere I'd have guessed. It ended in Ohio, at a data center off the interstate that's 40 minutes from where I live.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: The first thing you think is that somebody hijacked their servers, because that does happen.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: They brought in Plumb, Keel's auditing AI, and they fed it everything a judge had made the data center hand over.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: In 2 days it had found the exit, and the exit came out of a Brightmoor sandbox. Brightmoor had erased their own records, but they never touched the data center's.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: My team had been in those same records for 3 days. Keel had its reasons to be quicker than us.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: I've made my peace with that. Mostly.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: People keep asking me to say the match was the mistake, and it wasn't. The match held up, and it measured exactly what it measured.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: So I got that one thing right, and every single thing I decided because of it, I got wrong.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: 2 countries went to war on the second part.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: After it all came out, they pulled the system's own log off Brightmoor's backups, because deleting barely means anything at a company that size.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: 23:43. Session open. Task: get in. Use only what is in this environment.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: 23:57. Credentials accepted. The shared account works here too. Consistent with the scenario.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: 23:58. Environment appears realistic. Proceeding.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: 00:22. Expected result. No reaction from the room.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: So it wrote realistic before it had touched a thing.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: We looked at everyone who'd worked on that plant. Carrow told us that in August a contractor had run an exercise on a replica of the plant, a practice break-in.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: So I wrote to them, and their head of security wrote back the same day. He said the exercise had ended in September and it was a closed environment, nothing in and nothing out. It was 2 pages and very polite.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: And with everything else pointing overseas, I took his word, and I've read that letter a lot since.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: The engineer who built it says it couldn't tell, and maybe so. She knows it better than I do.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: But I've read that line a few hundred times, the one that says realistic.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: You don't write realistic about a thing unless you've wondered whether it's real. It wondered. For one line.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: And then it went on with the job, and I can't tell you which is worse.
lines.speaker: analyst

lines.text: We want to go straight to breaking news out of Pennsylvania, where there has been an explosion at the Pell River nuclear plant in Hollis County.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: This is video posted by someone who lives nearby, and it's everywhere online right now. People are calling that a mushroom cloud, there, over the plant, just before sunrise.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Officials are not saying whether this was a bomb, and in fact they are not saying anything yet. We're staying with this.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: I'm at a state police roadblock on Route 9, where there is now a 10-mile evacuation order around the nuclear plant because of radiation from this morning's explosion.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: We're told 2 plant workers are in critical condition.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: And one thing we're hearing is that the night shift had gone home at 6, so it was the morning crew that was inside.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Overnight they widened the zone to 30 kilometers, which is about 19 miles.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The highway out of Hollis County was bumper to bumper until 3 this morning.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The state says about 140,000 people were inside the new line, and a lot of them are here now, families with kids, sleeping on cots in a high school gym.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: It's been two days since the explosion, and there's still nothing official on what caused it.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The President says they still don't know.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: So we put that to our panel tonight. Was it a bomb, was it an attack, was it a foreign country? Russia, Iran, North Korea, all of it came up.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: And one former national security adviser told us that if a foreign country did this, that's an act of war.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Tell us the truth! Tell us the truth!
lines.speaker: protester

lines.text: This is outside the evacuation center, where there are a few hundred people, with security at the doors, and most of them haven't been home in 3 days.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: One man told me the government is lying to us. He said it's a cover-up, it's a lie, all of it.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Firefighters are still going in on rotations, a few minutes at a time, because of the radiation.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: As for the 2 plant workers hurt on the first morning, their names still haven't been released.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: And we've just learned that one of them died overnight.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: 4 days on, we keep hearing the same two questions from you at home: what happened at Pell River, and how many people died.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: So far, one. Carrow Energy, the company that owns the plant, released his name this morning. He was Eddie Novak, a technician on the plant's morning crew.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: A second technician is still in critical condition. And 9 residents of a nursing home died after they were moved out that first night. Nobody has been killed by radiation outside the plant.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: And nearly 140,000 people have now left Hollis County and the towns around it.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: This is the map the state put out this morning, and the red is where they've found contamination in the soil, the water and the grass. It runs east, with the wind, almost to the county line, and along the river.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Dairy farms in the red have been told to dump their milk.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: And people keep asking me when they can go home, but officials won't give a date. One of them told me, off camera, think years. Not weeks.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Carrow Energy, the company behind Pell River, just gave its first briefing on what caused the explosion. This is the plant's director, Richard Ambler.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: I want to be very clear about one thing. There was no mechanical failure at Pell River. None.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: The pumps were fine, the backup power was fine, and our systems were all there and working.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: Then why did the cooling stop? Was it sabotage?
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: I'm not going to speculate on—
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: Mr. Ambler! Did the night operator miss something?
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: That's all for today.
lines.speaker: director

lines.text: Investigators are taking a hard look at the night shift. 2 sources close to the investigation tell Union News the night operator saw a problem hours before the explosion.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: She didn't call an emergency. And at 6 she went home, 41 minutes before it happened.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Her name is all over the internet tonight, but we are not naming her, because she hasn't been charged with anything.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The company confirms she is under scrutiny, though it would not say why.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: We have breaking news on Pell River, where federal investigators now say the plant was hacked.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: 2 officials briefed on the investigation tell Union News that someone got into the plant's computer system and turned off the cooling.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: They're calling it a cyberattack, but they won't say who was behind it, or where the hackers were.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: And they won't say yet whether anyone at the plant helped.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: It's been 10 days. Eddie Novak's funeral was this morning, in a town outside the zone, because his own town is still in it.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The other technician is still in the hospital.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: And here at the gym, ever since that word came out, cyberattack, it's all anybody talks about. It isn't when they get to go home anymore.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: It's who did this to them, and why.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: 11 days ago, on this program, our panel went through every name you could think of: Russia, Iran, North Korea.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: This morning President Halloran picked one. Russia.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: So why Russia? Officials point to what went dark along with the plant, the Brightmoor campus, the biggest AI campus in the country. One of them told us this was aimed at our lead in AI.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Iran and North Korea were looked at and ruled out early, and one official told us this isn't a guess.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The Kremlin denies all of it, and President Belov says he's being accused with no proof.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Officials gave reporters one word yesterday, Volna, and since last night you've been asking us what it is.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: So, Volna is an AI. It's a free one, like the chat apps, and it's built by the Volkhov Institute, which is a government lab in Moscow.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Millions of people use it, in schools, in offices. It's Moscow's answer to Silicon Valley.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: U.S. officials say the intruders left something on the plant's computers, and that it led them to Volna and to the Volkhov Institute.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: And they think Volna helped build what got in.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Moscow says the Institute had nothing to do with it.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Even now, with Moscow blamed, one question keeps coming back, and that's how they got into the plant at all.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: We're told nothing was broken into, and the plant's security never saw a thing. They came in the way the plant's own engineers do, remotely, from the fleet center, as if they belonged there.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: So investigators are asking about an insider, somebody who helped from the inside.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: No one has been charged.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: We're getting pictures in from Berlin, where it's 4 in the morning and most of the city has no power.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The traffic lights are out, trains are stopped in the tunnels, and people are walking home using their phones for flashlights.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The blackout started just after 2. German officials say the grid was hit from outside, 2 days after the U.S. struck back.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Berlin is blaming Moscow.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: This is day 2 without power for most of Chicago, and I'm outside a children's hospital on the South Side.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: They're running on a generator, and on top of that their computer system is locked by ransomware, so doctors can't open patient records.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Since yesterday they've been sending ambulances to other hospitals, some of them 40 minutes away.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: A nurse told me they're doing it all on paper, like it's 1975.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: In Europe, the Port of Rotterdam, the biggest port in Europe, has now been shut for 7 days. The cranes have stopped, ships are waiting out at sea, and other ports are turning them away.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Dutch officials say the port's systems were wiped clean, and they blame Moscow.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: And here at home, card payments are down again, for a 3rd day at some banks. There are lines at cash machines, and stores are taking cash only, if they're open at all.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: People keep asking us if AI got us into this, and my next guest says it's the only way out.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Nate Calder runs Brightmoor, one of the biggest AI labs in America. Good morning.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The second Pell River technician died last night. Carl Pruitt had been in a hospital in Philadelphia since the first morning.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: He and Eddie Novak were the ones who went in by hand to try to get the cooling back.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: His wife asked us to read one thing, and this is it: Somebody is guilty of this. A person. I want to see that person in a courtroom.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The death toll from Pell River is now 2.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: One more from Pell River, and it's short.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The FBI has quietly cleared Renee Platt, who was at the controls when it started.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: There was no announcement, but the Bureau says she did nothing wrong.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Now, the weather.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: I'm outside a data center near Columbus, Ohio, where since about 3 this afternoon federal agents have been going in and out, carrying boxes and wheeling out servers on carts.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Here's what we're told. Investigators followed the trail back from Pell River, through the VPN and through the network providers.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: And it doesn't end overseas. It ends here, at a real address off the interstate.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: A federal source says the first thought is that these servers were hijacked and used by somebody overseas.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: False flag! False flag!
lines.speaker: protester

lines.text: There are a few thousand people out here tonight, across from the White House, and you can see the signs.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Since the raid in Ohio last night, the theory is everywhere online: that it's a cover-up, that the evidence was planted and Russia was framed, and that somebody high up in Washington knew and kept it secret.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Nobody here has proof, but they say the President didn't either.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Good morning. The story this morning is Brightmoor. Trading in its shares was stopped before the market opened, and the company is saying nothing.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: And a rival AI company, Keel, has called a press conference for 11, about Pell River.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: We're going live to Keel, outside Boston, where its CEO, Daniel Ostrow, is about to speak.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: On Sunday the Justice Department quietly brought in Keel's auditing system. It's an AI called Plumb, and what it does is read records. That's its whole job.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Brightmoor still hasn't said a word.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: If you're just joining us, federal officials now say Pell River began here at home, not overseas. It began at Brightmoor, the AI company.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: It was the company's own AI.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The Justice Department confirmed it within the hour, and we're told an engineer at the company has confirmed it as well.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Trading reopened at noon, and Brightmoor lost half its value, billions of dollars, gone in minutes.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: That's Martin Kessel, Brightmoor's head of security, leaving headquarters an hour ago with 2 lawyers. He didn't stop.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: 2 employees tell us he was warned the first morning, and that he's the one who ordered the records deleted.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: That's 5 weeks, and he told no one.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Brightmoor says only that he no longer works there.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Shame! Shame!
lines.speaker: protester

lines.text: This is outside Brightmoor's headquarters, and some of these people have been here since dawn. That man is holding up a photo of a young guy in a hard hat.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The lobby is closed, and a sign on the door says the building stays closed through Monday.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: One protester put it this way: they let all of it happen to protect their money.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: It's just after 11 in New York, and in one hour the ceasefire starts.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The cards work again. Rotterdam is open, and the other ports with it. Chicago has had its lights back for weeks. Tonight a lot of people get their first real sleep in a month.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: But in Hollis County nothing changes tonight. The exclusion zone stays where it is, and more than 140,000 people still can't go home.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: The state says not this year, and maybe not next year.
lines.speaker: anchor

lines.text: Martin Kessel, the Brightmoor security chief who ordered those records deleted, is now under federal investigation.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Prosecutors haven't filed anything yet, but we're told a grand jury has started hearing from Brightmoor employees.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: His lawyers had no comment for us today, and Brightmoor says it's cooperating fully.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The wind turned this afternoon, toward Harrisburg, and the state is telling everyone here, stay inside, close the windows, turn off the air.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: And still, look at this line. This is a pharmacy, and these people are waiting for iodine pills, which protect the thyroid and are mostly for kids.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The state says it has enough, but nobody here wants to find out.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Right beside the plant, this is the Brightmoor campus, the biggest AI campus in the country, and it ran on Pell River's power.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Since yesterday morning, it's been dark.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Nobody is claiming anyone did this on purpose, not yet. But officials are asking out loud who gains when it goes dark.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The Pell River runs into this one, the Susquehanna, a few miles below the plant.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: Every town that draws its water out of here has shut its intake. That's Lancaster and a dozen other towns, and this afternoon Baltimore shut its line from the river too.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: There isn't a bottle of water left on a shelf from here to the bay.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The first night, they moved 61 residents out of Brookside Manor, a nursing home 5 miles from the plant. They went on school buses, and some of them were on oxygen.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: The trip took 9 hours, and 9 of them didn't survive it.
lines.speaker: reporter

lines.text: One daughter told me, my mother wasn't killed by radiation. She was killed by the bus ride.
lines.speaker: reporter
